title: New Residential Sales — new single-family home sales (August 2026 data), 10:00 a.m. ET, the demand read the nowcast does not post
source: CENSUS: two independent census.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06. (1) economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes, 179 rows parsed), row "New Residential Sales | September 24, 2026 | 10:00 AM | August 2026", release code A202609241000, reference A202608. (2) construction/soc/schedule.html (HTTP 200, 59,625 bytes), the Survey of Construction program's own release-schedule table, whose "August 2026" row reads "September 17, 2026 | September 24, 2026" under the column header "(17th Workday) Revised Building Permits - 8:00 a.m. New Residential Sales - 10:00 a.m." — the same program-owned second primary the new-home-sales-2026-10-27 and -2026-11-25 lanes used. Promoted from the construction-spending-2026-10-01 lane's `estimate` proposal by this event's own initial research, on the precedent those lanes set: the no-self-confirm convention binds the discovering sweep, not the independent second look. Seven Census calendars (2020-2026, 1,135 unique rows) place this release on the 17th workday of the month after its reference month, and 2026-09-24 is the fifth consecutive on-schedule edition since the lapse backlog cleared on 2026-05-28. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED by the construction-spending-2026-10-01 adjacency sweep as the demand-side read of the same August 2026 reference month, seven days ahead of it. Initial research 2026-09-06 confirms the identity and then finds what separates this edition from every other 2026 edition of the series: THE PUBLIC NOWCAST CHANNEL IS CLOSED FOR IT. The Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx (HTTP 200, 16,944 bytes) puts new-home sales in the "other releases" column, not among the 8 triggers, and 2026-09-24 appears on the InternalUpdates sheet reading exactly "New-home sales" with NO PostedUpdates row — 7 of 12 2026 editions post, and this is the fourth consecutive internal-only one (06-24, 07-24, 08-25, 09-24). Measured on 1,822 same-quarter deltas from ContribArchives (1,871 vintages 2014-05-01 -> 2026-07-28), vintages dated on a New Residential Sales release move |delta residential| a median 0.0608pp against a 0.0066pp baseline (p<0.0001, 85.7% clearing 0.02pp vs 34.6%) — a real footprint that will leave no public trace on this date. The tape null replicates on eight instruments and 65 sessions since 2021 (SPY p=0.5571, QQQ p=0.3802, ITB p=0.4785, XHB p=0.3412, DHI p=0.8084, LEN p=0.4705, PHM p=0.9053, TOL p=0.3154, homebuilder ETFs narrower on release days), and the tempting starts-vs-sales asymmetry is a FALSE POSITIVE: unpaired, housing-starts sessions read XHB |ret| p=0.0204 and TOL p=0.0352, but paired by reference month (n=68 pairs, 2021+) every instrument lands at p>=0.05 and SPY is 51.5% coin-flip. The one directional claim this ledger does make is new to the family: July 2026 printed -10.5% m/m, and after any m/m <= -8% the next month's revised m/m is positive in 60 of 95 pooled (63.2%) and 14 of 21 since 2015 (66.7%), median +2.15%/+5.70%, against a ~49-52% unconditional base — a forecast with no instrument to express it. Lapse exposure is zero on every horizon this event has: it publishes inside a fiscal year already funded and FY2027 is funded to 2026-12-11 by PL 119-103; the exposed edition of this series is new-home-sales-2026-12-23, and the 2025 precedent is that a lapse ENDING 2025-11-12 still cost this series its 2025-12-23 slot (the 2025 calendar carries 9 New Residential Sales rows against 12 in each of 2020-2024). Impact LOW, symbols empty: no macro-keyed house playbook (0 hits, re-grepped 2026-09-06 across trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md) and no instrument attaches.
